headline: Meralco Refund Set Over Six Months; October Power Rates Still Rise
seoTitle: Meralco Refund Set Over Six Months; October Power Rates Still Rise
seoDescription: The ₱2.64-billion refund is expected from November. It is separate from the increase in October electricity rates.
deck: The ₱2.64-billion refund is expected from November. It is separate from the increase in October electricity rates.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What has been approved
paragraphs: The Energy Regulatory Commission has approved a provisional ₱2.64-billion Meralco refund over six months. Residential customers are due ₱0.1733 per kilowatt-hour, while the average across customer classes is ₱0.1020 per kWh, according to BusinessMirror and Power Philippines.

The adjustment concerns distribution charges collected from January through June 2026. Its amount remains subject to the regulator’s final evaluation. The six-month schedule is shorter than the 12 months sought by Meralco.

sections.heading: October bills still increase
paragraphs: The refund should not be read as a promise that total electricity bills will remain unchanged. Daily Tribune reported that Meralco’s October overall residential rate rose by ₱0.3191 per kWh to ₱15.0615 per kWh, driven by higher generation costs.

The additional refund is expected to begin in November. Implementation depends on the regulatory order and billing cycle; customers should check their own statement. A distribution-charge adjustment and a change in the total electricity rate are different measures.

sections.heading: What households can check
paragraphs: At 200 kWh, a ₱0.1733-per-kWh refund equals ₱34.66 for that billing period. This calculation concerns the refund alone: consumption, other charges and adjustments still affect the final bill.
Look for the refund entry on the statement and use Meralco’s official billing channels to query a missing or unclear adjustment.
